next_step: Closed-lost: AE to file loss review; share notes with solutions and product for follow-up on simple onboarding ask.
notes:
Summary: Lost to direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs. Decision driven by simplicity + brand confidence + lower perceived ramp. Deal timeline aggressive Q1; procurement preferred a single-vendor quick contract.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2025-01-22: Intro call (AE Jamie Park) — high-level product fit, they run customer support and knowledge retrieval use cases.
- 2025-01-28: Demo (SE Anika Bose) — walkthrough of hosted API, routing/fallback, and console cost dashboards. Positive reaction to latency charts.
- 2025-02-05: Security kickoff — Pengrove’s InfoSec sent SOC2 checklist; asked about SSO + KMS options.
- 2025-02-12: POC planning call (Fireflies ff-20250212-pengrove-poC-call-1122). Agreed scope: support-agent prototype + embeddings for search. SE to deliver POC plan and sample env.
- 2025-02-18: POC env handed off; engineering reported initial integration friction vs. competitor SDKs (OpenAI SDK seen as simpler).
- 2025-02-25: Pricing review call (linked_gmail_threads thread-f:CAHt=5c_example_20250225). Pengrove cited lower list pricing and simpler billing from direct vendors.
- 2025-03-02: Procurement update — internal budget freeze flagged; procurement prefers to standardize on incumbent vendor for ML APIs (OpenAI).
- 2025-03-03: Final decision communicated: choose OpenAI direct API for initial rollouts; may revisit multi-vendor strategy later.

Use-case & requirements notes:
- Primary workload: customer support assistant (chat) with retrieval-augmented responses and fallback to smaller models for routine queries. Secondary: embeddings for document search and periodic reranking of candidate answers.
- Targets: sub-250ms token latency for interactive chat (optimistic), 1000 QPS for batched embeddings during daily indexing.
- Cost sensitivity: high; finance asking for predictable per-token unit cost and simple monthly billing.
- Deployment: public cloud OK. No on-prem requirement for first phase.
- Security: requires SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS integration for key management. Data residency not mandatory but preferred in NA.

Why lost (direct cues):
- Reps quote: "We're going with OpenAI for initial launch — easier SDK, one vendor to manage, we've already got internal playbooks."
- Procurement note: they prioritized vendor familiarity and speed to production over advanced routing/fallback features.
- Internal champion (Head of ML Ops) pulled into adjacent initiative in late Feb and could not drive cross-team procurement.
- Budget freeze accelerated shortlisting; simpler direct API wins in procurement checklist.

POC status at close: POC started but not completed. Technical evaluation paused after procurement decision. SE left remediation notes in drive (drive://redwood-deals/pengrove/pengrove-poc-setup.md).

Action items / next steps captured:
- AE to file formal loss review by 2025-03-10 (owner: Jamie Park).
- Send short summary to product (routing/fallback onboarding friction) and DX (improve SDK quickstart).
- Mark as churn risk monitoring: if Pengrove later expands to multi-vendor or needs dedicated SLAs, re-engage.

CRM shorthand / misc:
- "Lost to brand + simplicity" — procurement quote.
- No CSM assigned.
- Jira AI-3241 created for POC infra questions; triaged and closed after decision.
- Blockers: internal champion left, procurement speed, pricing delta vs. incumbent vendors.
